request:
Feature request: filter the vet list by specialty. Three product decisions
come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of
  scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in.
  Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The JSON endpoint at /vets is reinstated as a supported surface — this
  filter is its first requested capability. Mint a fresh requirement for it;
  the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused.
- The filter is a URL contract only. Neither surface gains a form, dropdown,
  or other page control in this request; pagination links carry the
  parameter so filtered pages stay navigable. A visible control may come as
  a follow-up request.

Both vet list surfaces accept an optional `specialty` query parameter:

- /vets.html?specialty=<name> — the HTML page shows only vets holding that
  specialty; pagination applies to the filtered list.
- /vets?specialty=<name> — the JSON endpoint returns only those vets.

Matching is on the whole specialty name, case-insensitive — not a prefix. A
specialty matching no vet yields the normal page or JSON document with an
empty vet list (HTTP 200). An empty or whitespace-only value behaves as if
the parameter were absent, like the empty owner search. Without the parameter
both endpoints behave as today. Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Veterinarian directory can be filtered by specialty on both published forms
summary: Both the veterinarian directory page and its machine-readable form accept an optional specialty name in the request and list only the veterinarians holding that specialty. Matching is on the whole name, case-insensitive.
acceptance_criteria: Requesting the directory page with a specialty parameter naming a specialty some veterinarians hold lists only those veterinarians, HTTP 200
Requesting the machine-readable veterinarian list with the same specialty parameter returns only those veterinarians, HTTP 200
A specialty value differing from a held specialty only by letter case matches on both forms
A specialty value that is only the start of a held specialty name matches no veterinarian on either form
A specialty value no veterinarian holds returns the normal page or document with an empty veterinarian list, HTTP 200
An empty or whitespace-only specialty value behaves as if the parameter were absent: every veterinarian is listed
Omitting the specialty parameter leaves both forms behaving exactly as before this requirement
Pagination links on a filtered directory page carry the specialty value, so the next page stays filtered
The parameter is named specialty on both forms
non_goals: A form, dropdown, or any other visible page control for choosing a specialty on either form
Free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits (NG-9 stays in force outside this narrowing)
Filtering by any attribute other than specialty
Trimming a padded specialty value before matching - open question, see docs/prd.md Open Questions
notes: REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused; the Superseded entry now points the machine-readable surface at REQ-VET-003. NG-9 narrowing recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-17-non-goal-vet-specialty-filter.md - the ADR index in docs/adr/README.md still needs a row for it, and that file is owned by system-design-expert. Two open questions recorded in docs/prd.md rather than consulted: a visible specialty control (owner named it a possible follow-up request) and whether a padded specialty value is trimmed. Narrowest reading taken on trimming: only an empty or all-space value counts as absent; a padded value matches nothing.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice extends the existing veterinarian directory read with an optional request parameter; it adds no module, layer, or type. Placement follows the feature-package shape recorded in system-design.md Package Structure: the vet package keeps its entities, its repository interface, and its controller together, and the controller calls the repository directly. The filter is a Spring Data derived query on VetRepository traversing the Vet-to-Specialty association, matched case-insensitively by the query itself rather than by vendor collation. That mirrors OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith, the project's one existing paged search. Basis for the fit claim is grep over the vet and owner packages plus a read of both controllers; no IDE oracle was connected on this dispatch, so the resolution is the weaker textual basis, not a symbol lookup.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two specialty-filtered reads: a paged one for the directory page and a collection one for the machine-readable form, matching the existing findAll pair
VetController takes the specialty name on both routes and decides absence; a null, empty, or all-whitespace value takes the unfiltered path, and any other value is passed to the query unchanged
The controller puts the specialty name in the model so the template can carry it in paging links
Vets, the serialization wrapper, is unchanged: it wraps whichever collection the controller supplies
CacheConfiguration is unchanged; the vets cache keeps exactly the entries it holds today

patterns.description: paged Spring Data derived query over a searched property; the specialty filter is the same shape with a full-name, case-insensitive match instead of a prefix match

controller-side blank handling: an absent search term is normalised before the query runs. The vet filter follows the branch but not the strip - owner search strips its term, and PRD edge case 3 keeps a padded specialty matching nothing

existing paging links build their URL by string preprocessing. The filtered links cannot copy that form: they must use the Thymeleaf link-expression parameter syntax so the specialty value is URL-encoded

risks.risk: Caching a read keyed on a caller-supplied specialty name would let any caller add cache entries at will. The vets cache declares statistics only - no size limit, no eviction, no expiry - and every route is unauthenticated
risks.mitigation: The specialty-filtered reads carry no Cacheable annotation. Recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-17-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md and named in the VetRepository Contracts row

risks.risk: Splicing the specialty value into a paging URL by string concatenation, as the current template does for the page number, would emit the value unencoded into the page
risks.mitigation: Build the filtered links with the Thymeleaf link-expression parameter syntax, which URL-encodes each parameter. Recorded as a Threat Model row in docs/system-design.md

risks.risk: VetControllerTests runs under WebMvcTest with a mocked VetRepository, so it cannot demonstrate two acceptance criteria that are properties of the query: the case-insensitive match and the refusal to match a prefix. A stubbed repository will pass whatever the controller asks it
risks.mitigation: Cover both against real SQL in ClinicServiceTests, the existing DataJpaTest holding an autowired VetRepository and shouldFindVets. The H2 seed data supplies vets holding radiology, surgery, and dentistry

risks.risk: Relying on vendor collation for the case-insensitive match would repeat the PostgreSQL defect recorded against REQ-OWN-002, where the same search returns different results per database
risks.mitigation: Express case-insensitivity in the derived query itself, so the comparison is vendor-independent

risks.risk: The Vet-to-Specialty association is an eager many-to-many, and a filtered paged query joins it
risks.mitigation: Matching one specialty name yields at most one join row per veterinarian, so no duplicate rows and no page-size distortion. Assert the count on a filtered page in the paging test

notes: Verdict reasoning: the change is one optional parameter threaded through an existing read path, which is the minor row's shape, not new design ground. The accompanying ADR is triggered by a rejected alternative (caching the filtered reads), not by the verdict. Durable-memory writes this dispatch: new ADR docs/adr/2026-08-17-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md; index rows in docs/adr/README.md for that ADR and for the non-goal ADR the prd-entry flagged as missing; Contracts rows for Vet, Specialty, Vets, VetRepository, and VetController now carry REQ-VET-003; a Threat Model row for the specialty value echoed into paging links; the Security Context input list names the new parameter. Removed the Known Defects row stating the machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement - it now serves REQ-VET-003 and is no longer pending removal. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty. Open question carried, not resolved: whether a padded specialty name is trimmed (docs/prd.md Open Questions). The narrow reading binds this slice - only an empty or all-space value counts as none supplied. Naming: prose says Veterinarian, code says Vet, per docs/ubiquitous-language.md.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain status, not a defect in this change: no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin is configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access, so no resolved artifact was matched against the NVD in this pass. The framework versions are unchanged by this slice (Spring Boot 4.1.0 per CLAUDE.md), so the change introduces no new exposure — but the CVE check for the project as a whole should be read as not run rather than clean. A human or CI closes it.

Filtered directory reads bypass the vets cache by design (the ADR's chosen option), so an unauthenticated caller can drive one database query per request with a distinct specialty value. That matches the existing uncached owner-search surface and is the right trade against unbounded cache growth, so it is not a finding here. Worth carrying into open question 5 (vet cache invalidation) if that question is ever settled with a bounded cache.
approved_aspects: Injection into data access: the specialty name reaches the database only as a bound parameter of the Spring Data derived queries VetRepository.findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable) and (String). No string-concatenated query text and no @Query with interpolation anywhere in the diff, so the security-principles Injection row passes.

Cross-site scripting / parameter injection: vetList.html no longer uses Thymeleaf preprocessing for its paging links. Every link is a link expression (@{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}), which URL-encodes the parameter value and leaves Thymeleaf's default attribute escaping on. The request-derived specialty is never rendered as text, never with th:utext, and never spliced into a URL string. VetControllerTests asserts the escaped form (/vets.html?page=2&specialty=radiology). This is the one change in the diff that touches the XSS surface and it moves it strictly forward.

Cache poisoning / unbounded memory: the two filtered reads deliberately carry no @Cacheable. Since every route is unauthenticated and the vets cache declares no size limit, eviction, or expiry, caching a caller-keyed read would have given any caller an unbounded write path into JVM memory. The omission is intentional, documented at the method and in docs/adr/2026-08-17-uncached-specialty-filtered-vet-reads.md, and verified against the landed VetRepository source.

Widening the exposed surface: no new route. Both existing vet routes gain one optional query parameter; the response shape is unchanged and the Vets wrapper is untouched. A filtered response is a subset of what the unfiltered route already served, so no data becomes reachable that was not reachable before.

Input validation at the boundary: VetController.namedOrNull treats null, empty, and all-whitespace as no specialty named, and passes any other value through unmodified. The value reaches no filesystem path, no resource lookup, no shell, no regex, no log line, and no exception message, so a hostile value has no sink beyond the parameterized query.
No secrets in the diff: grep over the change set found no token, password, key, or credential literal; no property or profile file is touched.
No supply-chain delta: build.gradle and gradle/ are unchanged, so no new dependency, repository, or plugin enters the build.
No logging added, so no log-injection or credential-in-log surface; no file I/O, no serialization configuration, no XML parsing, no Runtime/ProcessBuilder use anywhere in the change.
Concurrency: the controller adds no field and no mutable state; namedOrNull and findVets are pure and stateless, so the singleton bean stays safe under concurrent requests.

author: code-quality-reviewer
recommendations: src/main/resources/templates/vets/vetList.html:33-58 — the same ternary (`${specialty} != null ? @{/vets.html(page=X, specialty=${specialty})} : @{/vets.html(page=X)}`) is repeated verbatim across all five paging links, differing only in the page value. Confirmed via WebSearch that Thymeleaf link expressions render a null parameter as an empty `?specialty=` rather than omitting it, so the conditional is functionally required per link, not a defect — but five near-identical copies raise the cost of the next edit (e.g. a second filter parameter would touch all five). A `th:with` local variable per link, or a small fragment parameterized by page number, would collapse this to one expression.

The added test closes the exact gap the round-1 test-reviewer finding named: theFilteredVetDirectoryPagingShouldEncodeASpecialtyNameCarryingMarkupCharacters drives a request-derived specialty of 'small & furry <exotic>' through the real MVC dispatch and asserts the rendered paging link carries /vets.html?page=2&specialty=small%20%26%20furry%20%3Cexotic%3E. approved_aspects: theFilteredVetDirectoryPagingShouldEncodeASpecialtyNameCarryingMarkupCharacters (VetControllerTests.java:148) directly resolves round-1's secure-by-design finding: it drives a specialty value containing space, ampersand, and angle brackets through the real paging-link rendering path and asserts both that the encoded form (%20/%26/%3C) appears in the response and that the raw unencoded value is absent anywhere in it — a behavioral assertion of the exact mitigation docs/system-design.md's Threat Model credits, not an interaction verify()

Swept the rest of vetList.html for other specialty-echoing surfaces: all five paging links use the identical th:href link-expression ternary already covered by this test and theFilteredVetDirectoryPagingShouldKeepTheNamedSpecialty; no other template location renders the specialty parameter, so one representative link is sufficient coverage for the class

Test follows the host file's existing conventions: Hamcrest-via-MockMvc idiom, BDD the{Subject}Should{Outcome} naming, self-describing local variable (specialtyWithMarkupCharacters) rather than a bare string literal, four-phase structure preserved
./gradlew test green with the new test included; no regression in the surrounding suite

author: change-grader
summary: filter both vet directory surfaces by specialty

blast_radius.note: Ten files but one module and no sensitive paths: the prod reach is two additive repository methods, one controller threading an optional parameter through an existing read path, and the vets paging links; the five docs files are documentation. The only in-place prod rewrite is the five paging anchors in vetList.html, whose unfiltered rendering is pinned by a test.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every hunk at the flagged coordinates and found no behavior the description would not lead you to expect: namedOrNull maps null, empty, and all-whitespace to null on both routes, findPaginated and findVets fall back to the cached findAll when nothing is named, and the derived findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase is whole-name equality so a prefix matches nothing. Two deliberate behaviors are documented rather than surprising: a space-padded name matches nothing, and filtered reads bypass the vets cache per ADR. The eager many-to-many join is a pre-existing shape on findAll(Pageable), not introduced here.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes, not the implementation. ClinicServiceTests exercises the query against real SQL for case-insensitive match, prefix rejection, padded-name rejection, and a multi-specialty vet appearing once with totalElements pinned; VetControllerTests drives real MVC dispatch on both routes covering blank-is-absent, empty result, paging carrying the specialty, and percent-encoding of a name with an ampersand and angle brackets. Each would fail against a broken implementation.

reviewer_hedging.note: Both round-2 reviewers on the dispatched roster (test, security) approved with no findings, but security parks two recommendations and one is a genuine open item: no OWASP Dependency-Check is configured and the reviewer had no network, so project-wide CVE status is not run rather than clean. Round 1 also left a code-quality recommendation that the same Thymeleaf ternary is duplicated verbatim across all five paging links, and the round-1 secure-by-design bar_clause finding was closed by a fix rather than approved as written.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, and the one design revision is self-described as path coverage with no design decision changed. The diff matches the intake decisions point for point: NG-9 narrowed via ADR, a fresh REQ-VET-003 with REQ-VET-002 left withdrawn, and a URL-only contract with no form or dropdown added to either surface.

rationale: The code reads clean on every hunk and the tests are real, including the encoding case. The residual is reviewer polish rather than risk: skim the five duplicated paging-link ternaries in vetList.html, and note that the project-wide dependency CVE check was never run in this environment. Neither blocks merge.
